confirmed.head: GUIDED DEMO · 2/6 A truck breaks down
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the returned twin state at simulated 17.17 h
confirmed.text: HT-01 has stopped (loading area, under the excavator). It is off the haul road, so no lane is blocked; the other five trucks keep working.

beforeConfirmation.status: Confirmed by the returned twin state at simulated 17.19 h
beforeConfirmation.text: With five trucks the twin still expects 770 t/h, because the excavator, not the fleet, sets the pace. This failure is off the road, so little is lost. The saved timeline (right) shows the costly case, a failure on the haul road: output dips while the lane is blocked, then recovers after the tow.

confirmed.head: GUIDED DEMO · 4/6 Switch on Smart Dispatch
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the returned twin state at simulated 17.22 h
confirmed.text: Smart Dispatch is on. The twin calculates that 4 trucks keep the excavator busy and 5 are available; 5 are cycling and 0 parked so far. Extra trucks park in the standby bay as they reach the face, engines off, and rejoin when needed.

beforeConfirmation.status: Confirmed by the returned twin state at simulated 17.24 h
beforeConfirmation.text: The saved, matched model run (right) compares both policies from one identical start: Smart Dispatch keeps the same output with fewer truck-hours per 1,000 t, because the excavator, not the number of trucks, limits production.
